through_line: Udaypur across its masters: the V.S. 1220 stone naming the Caulukya Kumārapāla and his mahāsādhanika at Udaypur (U1); Naravarman's frayed east, the mahākumāras at Vidisha, Caulukya governors, Vindhyavarman's return; Devapāla residing at Udayapura (1232), Iltutmish at Bhilsa, three-sided pressure, 1305; the Sam. 1366 title, the mosque of 1336–38 and the temple left in worship, the survival legends tested; temples turned to mosques at Vidisha, Ujjain and Dhār, Udayeśvara the exception; the Malwa sultans' Bhilsa and the 1488 mosque; Sarkar Chanderi, the translated farman, the Shahi Masjid of A.H. 1041 and the qāzī's claim (U7); Aurangzeb at Bhilsa in 1682, at Udaypur only in legend; Afghans and Marathas to Scindia by 1775; the brass cover (HELD, RR-2); Gwalior's district to Madhya Pradesh; the famine of 1899–1900 and the feeder road of 1905; political demotion dated step by step, economic decline undatable, the Gazetteer's 'once a place of considerable importance' into Chapter 11.
